findings.reason: the strip branch is now decided against, so its tolerance clause and the body sentence name a production parameter that does not exist; a worker on §3 has to infer that the 1e-13 floor is the whole tolerance, and the dead strip text is exactly the kind of surviving branch that sends a node looking for a width to implement.
findings.text: §3 done-when (1) measures the device-versus-host agreement "to within the largest per-slope rounding term §2 records at the production strip width (the worst slope, since the mesh mixes them)", and the §3 body states "The strip width is the edge-length fraction the sheet-route decision records" (line 242), but the `sheet-route` decision recorded at line 418 in this same change sets `data-choice="part-ii-sheet"` on the measured finding that "no single edge-length fraction meets 1e-10", so the decision records no edge-length fraction and §2 records no rounding term at a production width; the only clause that resolves the tolerance is the trailing "On the Part II branch there is no strip cancellation and the tolerance is the floor"
